text: The Authority signs a shale-gas lease with CNX. 18 percent of gross revenues and a signing bonus.
detail: Oil and Gas Lease executed Feb. 22, 2013, after the board awarded the drilling bid on Feb. 8. The signing bonus is reported four ways across the record, $45.1 million to $46.3 million, and is not printed as one figure.

speaker: Brad Penrod (Authority)
text: The airlines "were like little kids on a holiday morning"
detail: On the first fee cut funded from the gas bonus, as reported by the Post-Gazette.

text: Airline charge cut 55 cents, $14.66 to $14.11, out of the gas bonus, the Post-Gazette reports. Six more cuts follow.
detail: The first of seven annual reductions. Figures as reported by the Post-Gazette, July 16, 2013; the paper names the gas bonus as the source.

speaker: Rich Fitzgerald (County Executive)
text: "Us and some other airports are in a bad spot because we have the costs of a hub without the revenues of a hub."
detail: To TribLive, on the shale-gas fee reduction.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: "You need less space to heat, you need less space to cool, and we have to figure out what that right size looks like."
detail: Right-sizing is public a year before the landside replacement is approved. TribLive, Aug. 11, 2016.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: Cost per passenger "would actually fall from an average of $12.69 to $9.73" by 2023.
detail: At the vote approving the program at about $1.1 billion. Post-Gazette, Sept. 12, 2017.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: Renovating instead "is actually not cheaper and we looked at it."
detail: The alternatives claim, made once. No renovation figure has been published since. Post-Gazette, Sept. 12, 2017.

speaker: David Minnotte (board chairman)
text: "The people of Pittsburgh finally get an airport built for them and not US Air."
detail: Post-Gazette, Sept. 12, 2017.

speaker: Patrick Bowes (American Airlines)
text: "We feel very confident that we'll get there."
detail: On the $9.73 forecast. Post-Gazette, Sept. 12, 2017.

text: The board approves a new landside terminal at about $1.1 billion, the Post-Gazette reports. Under the residual agreement the airlines pay what other revenue does not cover.
detail: The program figure rests on a newspaper clip. Under the residual airline agreement the carriers pay whatever other revenue does not cover.

speaker: Allegheny Institute (unnamed consultant)
text: "You're going to spend $1.1 billion to save $23 million? What Wall Street person would ever make that decision?"
detail: Allegheny Institute for Public Policy, Oct. 4, 2017, three weeks after the vote.

speaker: Bob Kerlik (spokesman)
text: A project that "will use no local tax dollars" and "will lower costs."
detail: Post-Gazette, Feb. 20, 2018.

speaker: John Fiorita (former US Airways properties director)
text: "You're still going to have maintenance costs associated with the terminal. Have any of those numbers been taken into account?"
detail: Post-Gazette, Feb. 20, 2018.

speaker: John DeFazio (County Council president)
text: "We have no jurisdiction... We're not putting any money into it." No hearing is held.
detail: Post-Gazette, Feb. 20, 2018. County Council confirms every airport board member.

text: The sixth straight fee reduction, "subsidized in part by oil and gas revenues... and state gambling funds," the Post-Gazette reports. 2019 budget $10.35.
detail: Post-Gazette, Oct. 19, 2018, stating the mechanism outright.

text: Rental-car customer facility charge rises to $5.50 a day.
detail: From $3.00 at its start in March 2011.

text: The $150 million Gaming Act allotment is exhausted. A separate $12.4 million a year is expected to continue.
detail: ACAA annual report 2019: "Through February, 2019, the Authority has received $107.5 million of the original $150.0 million allotment bringing the total received by the County and Authority to $150.0 million." The report expects a further $12.4 million a year for as long as the Authority remains a recipient under the Act.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: "All of this has been very much in coordination with the airlines, whose needs have to be considered."
detail: On the unveiled designs. TribLive, Feb. 20, 2019.

speaker: Tasso Katselas (architect of the 1992 terminal)
text: Saying no taxpayer dollars will be used "is a cruel joke."
detail: Open letter to the board, April 2019. Clip, unused in the story.

text: Master Trust Indenture dated. The Coverage Account sits ninth in the flow of funds, "at the discretion of the Authority," capped at 25 percent.
detail: Dated as of Dec. 1, 2019 (Official Statement 2025A/B cover, PDF 1). The flow of funds is at Official Statement 2021A/B PDF 35 (printed 25); the cap at PDF 37 (printed 27).

text: The Airline Operating Agreement takes effect. Residual: the carriers pay whatever other income does not cover.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 70. Effective Jan. 1, 2020, expiring Dec. 31, 2028, extendable three years only by mutual agreement.

text: Customer facility charge rises to $6.00 a day.
detail: CNX terminates the Allegheny County Airport portion of the lease the same month.

text: Gaming revenue $12,400,000 in 2020, and exactly that in each of the next four years.
detail: ACAA annual reports 2020 through 2024.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: "By keeping our operations running smoothly, we will be in a position to rebound along with our airline partners."
detail: As airlines cut flights at the start of the pandemic. TribLive, March 17, 2020.

text: $19.1 million of federal pandemic relief designated into the pledge: CARES, CRRSA and ARPA.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, Exhibit E, PDF 316. Gas is designated at zero in every year from 2020.

speaker: Tasso Katselas (architect of the 1992 terminal)
text: "There's no way anyone can justify it that has any sense."
detail: Post-Gazette, June 24, 2021, as the airline agreement is extended to 2028.

text: The airline agreement is extended to Dec. 31, 2028.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 70.

text: The board resolution authorising the terminal bonds. The minutes for this meeting are missing.
detail: Board agenda, July 16, 2021. Item 9, public comment.

text: LeighFisher's first coverage forecast. Two of four years in the base case and four of four in the slow case fall below 1.25 on net revenues alone, by this record's arithmetic.
detail: Official Statement 2021A/B, PDF 185 (printed B-19). Seven of the eight computed years assume the Coverage Account at its 25 percent ceiling. The letter is signed LEIGHFISHER with no individual name.
short: First forecast: 2 of 4 base, 4 of 4 slow years below 1.25 on net revenues alone. Ours.

text: The first terminal bonds are sold. Interest is capitalized, so nothing enters the airline charge for four years.
detail: Official Statement 2021A/B. The $832.7 million total is available only as an attributed clip figure.
short: The first terminal bonds are sold. Interest is capitalized for four years.

speaker: Eric Sprys (chief financial officer)
text: The cost per passenger "should end up in the range of $10 to $11."
detail: At the groundbreaking. Post-Gazette, Oct. 14, 2021. Two months earlier the bond statement had printed $12.92 base and $16.07 slow for 2025, and $13.47 base and $16.63 slow for 2026.

speaker: David Minnotte (board chairman)
text: "A more suitable terminal with lower costs."
detail: At the groundbreaking. Post-Gazette, Oct. 14, 2021.

text: FAA approves $633.4 million in passenger facility charges for the program.
detail: The application number and record of decision are not in the file.

text: The CNX lease is amended. CNX may take deductions, which "resulted in a reduction in the total percentage of revenues received by the Authority."
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B. In exchange, a seven-year drilling commitment.

text: Federal pandemic relief designated again in 2022. Nothing from gas; nothing from gaming.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, Exhibit E, PDF 316.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: "This is going to make life a lot better for people who travel and everyone who uses the airport."
detail: On the $1.4 billion terminal. TribLive, Sept. 28, 2022.

text: Federal relief designated for the last time. The statement gives two figures for 2023, $4,040k at Exhibit E and $3,029k at PDF 61.
detail: Both figures are disclosed; neither is chosen.

text: The Authority settles with its former concessionaire for $10,500,000.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B. Under the residual agreement, costs not covered elsewhere reach the airline rate base.

text: The 2023 bonds are delivered. Program cost now $1.57 billion. Demolition budgeted at $33 million. Opening "early 2025."
detail: Official Statement 2023A/B/C, dated Oct. 12, 2023.
short: The 2023 bonds are delivered. Program cost now $1.57 billion. Opening "early 2025."

text: The airlines approve a further $78 million for the airside renovation.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B.

speaker: Bob Kerlik (spokesman)
text: "Now the hub is gone, but the number of the people using the security checkpoint has about doubled."
detail: TribLive, July 2, 2024.

text: Spirit Airlines files for Chapter 11. Spirit was 9.7 percent of 2024 boardings.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B. Spirit ends Pittsburgh service in May 2026.

text: Customer facility charge rises to $8.00 a day.
detail: From $6.00. The line is printed on every rental receipt.

text: The airlines vote. The Authority commits at least $11.575 million a year of gaming money for 2026 through 2028, and waives a $5 million annual deposit.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 287 (printed B-101). The vote record, the notice and the tally are not in the file.
short: Airlines vote; the Authority commits $11.575 million a year of gaming money through 2028.

text: A further $82 million of airline approval brings the airline-approved ceiling to $1.7 billion.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 72 (printed 62).

speaker: Kroll Bond Rating Agency
text: A credit strength: "unique non-aviation revenue sources which can be applied on a discretionary basis." A challenge: a rising charge "could discourage service expansion or retention."
detail: KBRA rating report on the 2025 bonds, April 1, 2025. The Authority pays for the rating.

text: LeighFisher's second forecast. Five of six years fall below 1.25 on net revenues alone, by this record's arithmetic. Cost per passenger $19.13 in 2026, $20.53 by 2030.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 202 (printed B-16). Five of six years assume the Coverage Account at its ceiling. The gap runs $5.59 million to $11.72 million a year.
short: Second forecast: on net revenues alone, 5 of 6 years fall below 1.25. Division ours.

speaker: Seth Lehman (Fitch Ratings)
text: The borrowing "will drive Pittsburgh's cost per enplanement above A-rated airport standards."
detail: The Bond Buyer, April 21, 2025.

text: The 2025 bonds are sold, $410.5 million across two series, this record's sum of the par amounts. Program cost $1.7 billion. Demolition $0, postponed "to reduce project costs and associated debt."
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, dated April 22, 2025. Par amounts at PDF 2, the combined schedule at PDF 39. Contingency down from $123.1 million to $21.6 million, on "certain contractor bid overages."
short: The 2025 bonds are sold, $410.5 million across two series, our sum. Demolition $0.

text: Gaming money designated again, $8.17 million, the first designation of any kind since 2023.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, Exhibit E, PDF 316. From 2025 the designated line is entirely Gaming Act money.

speaker: Sara Innamorato (County Executive)
text: The terminal is an "economic jet engine."
detail: At the ribbon cutting, with the federal government shut down and the state budget 103 days overdue. Post-Gazette, Oct. 11, 2025.

speaker: Rep. Mike Kelly
text: "This project is an incredible example of when people work together, people that have the same vision with the same purpose."
detail: Seated between Democratic Reps. Chris Deluzio and Summer Lee. Post-Gazette, Oct. 11, 2025.

speaker: Gov. Josh Shapiro
text: The state does "find common ground every single day."
detail: Post-Gazette, Oct. 11, 2025. No speaker said what the building cost or who would pay for it.

speaker: Christina Cassotis (chief executive)
text: "This is a new day for our region. This is an airport built for Pittsburgh, by Pittsburgh."
detail: TribLive, Nov. 10, 2025, as the terminal opens.

text: Debt service enters the airline rate base: $54.4 million, after reading zero for five years. The billed charge goes from $11.77 to $17.01, up 44.5 percent.
detail: ACAA audited annual report 2025, Table IV, PDF 72 ($54,413,945); Table III, PDF 70. The per-passenger figures are this record's division.
short: Debt service enters the airline rate base: $54.4 million, after five years at zero.

text: Rates effective: $298.36 a square foot of terminal space, $4.06 per 1,000 pounds landed. Passenger facility charge $4.50.
detail: The Authority's published rate card, January 2026.

speaker: David Castelveter (former US Airways spokesman)
text: "Airlines don't eat costs."
detail: Post-Gazette, Jan. 11, 2026. Carriers have a "fiduciary responsibility" to pass expenses along, he said.

speaker: Michael Boyd (aviation consultant)
text: "Find me one major airport project in the USA that has ever been completed right on the original budget. It doesn't happen."
detail: Post-Gazette, Jan. 11, 2026. Carriers do not set prices airport by airport, he said.

speaker: The Authority (to the Post-Gazette)
text: The airport expects the charge to rise to $17.64 this year, from a pre-pandemic $9.77 in 2019.
detail: Post-Gazette, Jan. 11, 2026. The bond statement filed for investors nine months earlier printed $19.13 for the same year.

speaker: Bob Kerlik (spokesman)
text: "Nowadays, 98% of the airport's traffic is origin and destination."
detail: Post-Gazette, Jan. 11, 2026.

text: The Authority issues its passenger facility charge amendment notice. Comments due June 27.
detail: PFC amendment notice, May 27, 2026.

text: Annual debt service reaches $111.3 million a year, before passenger facility charges are netted.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 202.

text: The airline agreement expires. The $11.575 million gaming commitment ends. The $5 million waiver ends.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 70 and PDF 287. A three-year extension exists only if both sides want one.

text: Forecast airline cost per passenger $20.53, past every one of those expiries.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 202 (printed B-16). The forecast stops here; it is the end of the horizon, not a peak.

text: The bonds mature, 28 years after the airline agreement and the gaming commitment end.
detail: Official Statement 2025A/B, PDF 39: combined schedule to 2056, $3,232,650,565.
